logbook.hint: From/to dates are inclusive. Unknown style finds missing, blank, or literal Unknown route styles, even with an ascent protection override; Other finds present, unsupported route styles. Route grade min/max use your display system and exclude boulders (filter style for those). Missing route data finds routes without a recorded height, bolt count, or cached pitch list after route info was fetched. No pitch list cached also matches single-pitch and boulder routes when theCrag omits pitches, so it is not a list of multipitch routes missing data. The pitch-list filter excludes routes whose route info was never fetched (History not checked is a separate, route-history filter); Tag contains searches tag names; Exact tag matches Category:Name (case-insensitive, repeat `tagExact` in the URL for AND). Categories include Rock type, Steepness, Aspect, Style, Weather, Walk in time, Legality, and Condition when shown on chips. Project filters exclude unknown flags. No setter credit found includes routes whose history has not been imported. Weather filters use the opt-in Open-Meteo cache and only match outdoor ascents with cached weather for that day; the owner can also list outdoor ascents with no weather cached yet.

projectDetail.estimateNoAttemptData: Not enough comparable projects for an attempt estimate.
projectDetail.estimateNoSessionData: Not enough comparable projects for a session estimate.
projectDetail.hintExcludedEntries: {count} entries with missing, invalid or future dates are excluded from progression and estimates.
projectDetail.leadHistoricalComparison: Historical comparison: {count} completed outdoor projects in the same discipline and scale, within one grade step. Session and attempt estimates need at least three projects that took more work than you have logged so far.
projectDetail.leadNewestFirst: Newest first. Attempt counts on send entries include the successful try and can overlap separately logged failures.
projectDetail.leadReadinessRecalculated: Readiness is recalculated using evidence available by each climbing day. Logged effort measures practice, not moves completed.
projectDetail.leadSupportingPyramid: Supporting pyramid in the past 365 days, in this discipline and grade scale: {n1}/2 distinct routes one grade step below; {n2}/4 two steps below.
projectDetail.methodPoints: Up to 15 points come from unsuccessful tries on this project, against a soft target of 15 (short-term), 35 (medium) or 75 (long-haul). The horizon follows the gap to your best recent send: at most one step, two steps, or more. The base model caps at 94%. The first session establishes the baseline; each additional valid climbing day on this route adds one readiness point, up to 99%. Only a logged send reaches 100%. An unknown grade has no readiness estimate.
projectDetail.methodRanges: Remaining-work ranges are the middle half of your comparable completed projects, after subtracting your logged work. At least three longer projects are required for each range; estimates disappear when there is too little evidence or you have exceeded that history. These are personal historical comparisons, with no claim of scientific validation.
projectDetail.methodReadiness: Readiness uses the past 365 days of outdoor sends on distinct routes in the same discipline and grade scale. A best send at this grade or above contributes 60 points, one step below 35, or two steps below 10. Up to 20 points come from two routes one step below, and 25 from four routes two steps below.
projectDetail.methodSessions: One session is one valid written calendar day. Failed tries use the logged attempt count, or one when missing. A send count includes its successful try; its implied failures and separate failure entries use the larger total to avoid double counting. Invalid and future dates do not contribute to estimates. Private comments are never used.
projectDetail.noteProjectSent: This project is sent. The session history below records the work and later repeats.
projectDetail.noteRoughComparison: This is a rough comparison with completed projects, not a prediction. Unsent projects and unlogged tries are absent; a send can come earlier or much later.

weatherLocations.emptyNoMatchingPlaces: No matching places. Try a nearby town with its region.
weatherLocations.labelChosenFallback: Chosen fallback: {name}. Precise route/crag points still take priority.
weatherLocations.leadLocationPriority: Route points take priority, then crag points, then immediate sector points. Validated small area polygons supply an approximate boundary coordinate when these points are missing. Country centres are excluded when the original payload identifies them. Without a usable point, choose a nearby town as an approximate weather location. Polygon and town fallbacks do not move route maps or unlock weather badges. Existing weather stays cached, but only the current location's key is used.
weatherLocations.leadSearchPrivacy: Search sends only the place name and country code you enter to Open-Meteo/GeoNames when you submit. No ascent details or private notes are sent. Results are cached for 30 days; no place is selected automatically.
